Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother, has revealed that she was glad Portugal suffered a heavy defeat against Denmark following her son’s international retirement. Portugal were beaten 4-1 by Denmark in their first match since Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football on November 5. Ronaldo, 41, brought an end to his international career after representing Portugal for several years, making 234 appearances and scoring 146 goals. His retirement came less than a month after he was handed a 30-day suspension and fined £215 for walking out of the Portugal camp in September after learning that he would not start their Nations League encounter against Denmark. As reported by BBC Sport, speaking at a Sporting event on Monday, Aveiro was asked about her son’s decision to retire from international football. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources She admitted that Ronaldo was unhappy with the situation and claimed that he had been deceived. “Of course he was sad. They deceived him. And I’m sad, too,” she said. Reacting to Portugal’s 4-1 defeat against Denmark, she added: “The defeat was well-deserved. I was actually glad.” Meanwhile, Portugal coach Jorge Jesus was asked about Aveiro’s comments ahead of Portugal’s Nations League clash against Wales in Cardiff on Tuesday. The Portuguese manager appeared surprised that he was expected to respond to comments made by Ronaldo’s mother. “Now I have to respond to Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother?” Jesus said. “She is a lady I greatly respect. She suffered a lot to raise her children.” Asked whether the debate surrounding Ronaldo’s international retirement would eventually come to an end, Jesus admitted that he was unsure. “I don’t know when it’s going to stop. If you guys ask the questions, I have to answer. If you ask about Ronaldo next year, I will answer,” he added. Portugal will now turn their attention to their encounter against Wales as discussions surrounding Ronaldo’s departure from the national team continue.
